title: Sandbox-to-Scale: Framing and Pricing Notes for Developer Onramp
content:
Purpose:
This is a working brief to unify messaging for the developer "Sandbox-to-Scale" experience: how we describe the hosted API value prop, the rapid-try quickstart, and the pricing language that reduces billing anxiety while still nudging predictable adoption.

Goals (what this doc should help us decide):
- Concise microcopy and two landing-one-liners for the sandbox product block.
- Three quickstart flows (30s, 5min, 1hr) with suggested copy and success metrics.
- Pricing tier names + sample anchor language (for UX & marketing).
- Competitive differentiators we should call out in 1–2 lines.
- Questions / experiments to A/B during the next 6 weeks.

Audience: technical buyers (engineers, platform teams) evaluating hosted inference for production and early prototypes. Tone should be pragmatic, metric-driven, and engineer-friendly (no puff).

Core narrative (single paragraph).
Sandbox-to-Scale narrative draft: "Start with zero friction: get credentialed, run a sample model in seconds, and only pay when you push real traffic. As you grow, move from a cost-transparent metered plan to committed capacity with predictable latency and SLAs — same API, same tooling, different economics."

Developer-first value props (short bullets for UI / hero card):
- Instant dev loop: auth + first inference in under 60s, SDK examples for the language you use.
- Cost visibility: per-request cost shown in the console and explaining token vs embedding billing.
- Same interface from prototype to production: code you write in the sandbox is compatible with Dedicated / Private deployments.
- Fail-safe rollouts: canary model switches and automatic fallbacks built in.

Quickstart flows (copy + success metrics):
1) 30s "hello world" (for docs/CTA)
   - Copy: "Try a model now — paste a prompt, get a reply in seconds. No credit card to start."
   - Flow: Single-button demo in docs -> ephemeral API key -> sample prompt -> streaming response.
   - Success metric: percent of visitors who hit /playground -> first-response in <3s.

2) 5min "ship a prototype" (for onboarding checklist)
   - Copy: "From editor to demo in 5 minutes: example app, SDK snippets, and deployment hints."
   - Flow: repo template + single config file + environment variable for API key -> run -> test.
   - Success metric: % of signups that create a project and send >100 tokens within 72 hours.

3) 1hr "real testbed" (for early customers)
   - Copy: "Validate latency and cost for your workload — simulate requests and compare model variants."
   - Flow: guided benchmark runner in console, token-cost estimation, suggested model + quantization profile.
   - Success metric: trials that convert to paid within 30 days and run a pipeline benchmark.

Pricing-language drafts (microcopy + anchors):
- Sandbox (Free): "Free sandbox — 50k inference tokens, ephemeral API key, no card. Ideal for experiments and quick demos."
- Pay-as-you-go (PAYG): "Metered: pay only for what you use. Per-token pricing and per-embedding billing visible in console. No long-term commitment."
- Committed (Reserved): "Reserved capacity — predictable monthly invoice, lower per-token rates, optional burst pool. Best for production apps that need consistent latency."
- Enterprise (Private): "Private deployments with SLAs, support, and enterprise billing — tailored contracts."

Pricing phrasing tests (language variants to experiment):
- Variant A: emphasize "No surprises" — show sample invoice and monthly estimate.
- Variant B: emphasize "Scale discounts" — highlight percent savings when committing.
- Variant C: emphasize "Developer-first" — reduce friction copy, defer billing questions until conversion steps.

Anchors & examples to show in UI (small snippets):
- "Estimated cost for 100k tokens: $X (based on model: x-small)"
- "Sandbox credits remaining: 32,500"
- "Switch to Reserved to lower per-token cost by ~30%"

One-line competitive differentiators (suitable for a bullets block):
- "Same API from playground to private deployment — you won’t rewrite your integration."
- "Token-level cost breakdown in the console — see where your spend goes."
- "Built-in fallback routing keeps your app online when a variant runs out of capacity."

Quick competitor notes (callouts we should avoid copying word-for-word):
- Vendor X: strong brand recognition but opaque pricing and limited model catalog.
- Vendor Y: low-latency promise but complex upgrade path from trial to reserved capacity.
- OSS runtimes: great control and lower unit-cost for big teams but heavy ops burden and fragmented tooling.

Suggested page/module structure (console / marketing):
- Top hero: 1-liner + sandbox CTA + quick cost estimator.
- How it works: 3-step graphic (sandbox -> validate -> reserve).
- Pricing strip: sandbox, PAYG, reserved, enterprise — each with 1-liner and CTA.
- Quickstart cards: 30s/5min/1hr with badges.
- Social proof / benchmarks: dev testimonials + simple charts (latency vs cost for common models).

Measurement plan (what to instrument in the onramp):
- Sandbox activation rate (signup -> ephemeral key -> first inference).
- Time-to-first-inference (median).
- Conversion funnel: sandbox -> PAYG -> Reserved (30/60/90 day cohorts).
- Cost-per-conversion (marketing channel and referral).

Open questions & experiment backlog:
- Should sandbox require email confirmation or be fully anonymous? pros: lower friction; cons: harder to convert.
- Free credits vs token cap: do users respond better to 'X free tokens' or 'Y days of unlimited sandbox'?
- When to surface reserved pricing? immediate on signup, or after usage pattern detected?
- Messaging test: "No card needed" vs "Fast sign-up with card" — measure onboarding friction and fraud.

Copy snippets for UX (short):
- CTA: "Try the sandbox — no card required"
- Console badge: "50k free tokens included"
- Pricing modal headline: "Choose how you want to pay: meter or reserve"

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Draft hero microcopy for new landing (Ayesha) — due: 2025-11-09.
- Implement sandbox token UI in console (Product/Eng) — spike by 2025-11-23.
- Run A/B on "no card" vs "card" for new signups (Growth) — start 2025-12-01, 4-week test.

Notes / brainstorm fragments (raw):
- Consider showing an example monthly invoice early in the flow to build trust.
- For early customers, offer a temporary reserved discount (30 days) to reduce switching friction.
- SDK samples should include cost annotations inline so devs see the economics while coding.
- Keep phrasing plain: avoid legalese in pricing snippets.

End of brief.

(Internal: save iterations as sandbox-pricing-v1/v2/v3 in this folder. Major changes should call out the A/B IDs.)
